text: Splay, access, makeRoot, link, cut, path XOR.

A link-cut tree (LCT, 动态树) maintains a forest that changes: link two trees with an edge, cut an edge, and ask about paths (sum, XOR, max) in O(log n) amortised. It splits each tree into preferred paths, each stored in a splay tree ordered by depth.

Core operation access(x): make the path from the root to x one preferred path. With makeRoot(x) (access, then reverse that path) any path x–y becomes one splay tree: makeRoot(x), access(y), splay(y), and y's subtree aggregate is the path answer. Link and cut are a few lines on top.

30 void access(int x) { for (int last = 0; x; last = x, x = fa[x]) { splay(x); ch[x][1] = last; up(x); } } 31 void makeRoot(int x) { access(x); splay(x); flip(x); } 32 int findRoot(int x) { access(x); splay(x); while (ch[x][0]) { down(x); x = ch[x][0]; } splay(x); return

Template (P3690): XOR along a path, link, cut, change a value. The second test links 1–2–3 (1 ⊕ 2 ⊕ 3 = 0), cuts 1–2, then 2 ⊕ 3 = 1, and after setting node 3 to 5: 2 ⊕ 5 = 7.

Push reverse flags from the top of the splay tree down before splaying (pushAll); check that an edge really exists before cutting; and use isRoot (root of the splay tree), not "fa == 0", inside rotate and splay.

When an LCT is overkill: if the forest only grows, use DSU; if the tree is fixed, use HLD (进阶篇第9章); if queries are offline, segment-tree-on-time with a rollback DSU often works. LCT is the tool for online link and cut (洞穴勘测 P2147, 弹飞绵羊 P3203, Tree II P1501 with two lazy tags).
